character_sheet: The Baby Dragon is the Dragon's rig at less than half size with a hatchling's stats: a separate registry (ModEntities.java:496-497) whose class is a Dragon subclass (BabyDragon.java:29) — 50 HP and 5 attack (:41-48); the 0.30 speed there is overridden to the adult's 0.32 by Dragon's constructor (Dragon.java:133) — that inherits the whole adult AI, flight, combat and taming stack (:24-27) and is born with a small fire (the fire level defaults to 1, Dragon.java:190). The rig is the adult's: a three-block body with three back spikes, a two-piece neck to a horned head with an upper and a hinged lower jaw, two wings of three spars and three membrane panels each on a root panel, four legs and a seven-segment spiked tail ending in a fin (ModelDragon.createBodyLayer, ModelDragon.java:136-415). On the ground it sits, follows, is tempted by beef, wanders and hunts monsters, Mothra and the Kraken (Dragon.java:140-170, :942-957); in the air (DATA_ACTIVITY 1) it flies to a target, bites within five blocks plus half the target's width and, with fire, shoots small fireballs (handleAIFlight :670-706, shootProjectileAt :808-832). Beef tames it one time in five and an owner can mount it (:974-1005). It has no natural spawn entry in the port's data (the adult spawns in the Island biome). Read it as the adult's motion scaled down — the same stride, beat and tail, quicker and lighter.
size_notes: Drawn at x0.45 of the rig (BabyDragonRenderer.java:34, applied :44; shadow 0.6) on the shared 256x128 sheet (ModelDragon.java:415), dragon.png or white_dragon.png by the dragon type (BabyDragonRenderer.java:26-29); 1.0 x 1.4 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:496-497). The wings, legs, neck and tail are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.6 x the TRUE horizontal speed in blocks per tick (from xOld / zOld, not limbSwingAmount; about 0.6 rad at the 0.32 walk), zero below a limbSwingAmount of 0.001: every piece of a leg swings together about its rest (front upper ±0.557, front lower ∓0.557, hind thigh −0.632, shin 0.89, ankle −0.557, feet 0), the front left and hind right one way, the front right and hind left the other; in flight (activity 1) every leg is held tucked one radian and still
groups.plain: on the ground the four legs stride diagonally with the real speed, each leg a stiff chain; in the air they all tuck and hold
groups.math: a = amount > 0.001 ? cos(t * 1.25) * pi * |velocity_xz| * 0.6 : 0; activity != 0 ? (leg4 = 0.557 - 1, leg5 = -0.557 - 1, foot2 = -1, leg3 = 0.557 - 1, leg6 = -0.557 - 1, foot1 = -1, leg2 = -0.632 + 1, leg7 = 0.89 + 1, leg10 = -0.557 + 1, foot3 = 1, leg1 = -0.632 + 1, leg9 = 0.89 + 1, leg11 = -0.557 + 1, foot4 = 1) : (leg4/leg5/foot2 = rest + a; leg3/leg6/foot1 = rest - a; leg2/leg7/leg10/foot3 = rest - a; leg1/leg9/leg11/foot4 = rest + a)
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ACTIVITY byte (Dragon.java:66; 1 in flight) selects tucked-and-still over the stride
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.25 (ANIM_SPEED 1.0): the natural period is 2 pi / 1.25 = 5.03 ticks; the amplitude is the entity's real speed, so the reference clip's fixed limbSwingAmount does not drive it

groups.name: wings
groups.amplitude: in flight (activity 1): pi x 0.28 = 0.88 rad (50 deg) about zero at 0.75 rad/tick; on the ground and attacking: pi x 0.2 = 0.628 rad (36 deg) about −0.45 at 0.85 rad/tick; on the ground and calm: pi x 0.028 = 0.088 rad (5 deg) about −0.85 at 0.2 rad/tick; the root spar and root panel take the wave, the middle spar and inner membrane 4/3 of it, the tip spar and its two membranes 3/2, each placed at the end of the spar before; the right wing the negative
groups.plain: the wings beat wide and slow in flight, hang folded with a faint stir on the ground, and half-raise and flap while attacking on the ground; the beat widens from root to tip
groups.math: w = activity != 0 ? cos(t * 0.75) * pi * 0.28 : (attacking ? -0.45 + cos(t * 0.85) * pi * 0.2 : -0.85 + cos(t * 0.2) * pi * 0.028); wing1.zRot = wing15.zRot = w; wing3.zRot = wing8.zRot = 4w/3; wing2.zRot = wing7.zRot = wing9.zRot = 3w/2; wing4/wing14 = -w; wing5/wing10 = -4w/3; wing6/wing11/wing12 = -3w/2; positions along the spars by sin/cos x 7 and 6
groups.phase: three branches: DATA_ACTIVITY 1 (flying), else DATA_ATTACKING set / clear
groups.omega_note: the classic phase in flight is ageInTicks x 0.75 (period 8.38 ticks); ground attacking 0.85 (7.39 ticks); ground calm 0.2 (31.4 ticks)

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: segment 1: pi x 0.04 = 0.126 rad (7 deg); the segments behind: pi x amp x 0.125 / 0.25 / 0.375 / 0.5 / 0.625 / 0.75 in order (tail2, neck1, tail3, tail4, tail6, tail5) with amp 0.45 in calm flight (up to 61 deg at the tip) at 0.76 rad/tick, amp 0.75 attacking at 0.96 rad/tick, amp 0.22 on the ground and calm at 0.22 rad/tick, zero in the sitting pose; every segment in phase, placed at the end of the one before; the spikes ride their segments
groups.plain: the tail sways side to side, the swing growing toward the tip — brisk and wide in flight or when attacking, small and slow on the ground, still when sitting
groups.math: ts, amp = attacking ? (0.96, 0.75) : (activity == 0 ? (0.22, 0.22) : (0.76, 0.45)); sitting ? (0, 0); tail1.yRot = cos(t * ts) * pi * 0.04; tail2.yRot = cos(t * ts) * pi * amp * 0.125; neck1 = ... * 0.25; tail3 = ... * 0.375; tail4 = ... * 0.5; tail6 = ... * 0.625; tail5 = ... * 0.75; spike10/7/8/3/9 = the segment they ride; positions along the chain by cos/sin x 6
groups.phase: state-branching: attacking, or the calm ground state, or sitting (isInSittingPose) select the rate and width
groups.omega_note: the classic phase in calm flight is ageInTicks x 0.76 (period 8.27 ticks); attacking 0.96 (6.54 ticks); calm on the ground 0.22 (28.6 ticks)

groups.name: mouth
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.14 = 0.44 rad (25 deg) about 0.4; not attacking: still at 0.07
groups.plain: the lower jaw chomps fast while the attacking flag is set and hangs nearly shut otherwise
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (Dragon.java:64; set at :685 with a target in flight, :588 ridden) selects
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 1.5: the natural period is 4.19 ticks

behaviour: The Baby Dragon runs the adult's model code at 0.45 scale (BabyDragonRenderer.java:34): on the ground the four legs stride diagonally at 1.25 rad/tick (a 5-tick period), each leg a stiff chain, the swing scaled by the entity's TRUE horizontal speed (from its last position, ModelDragon.java:425-432) rather than by limbSwingAmount; in flight (DATA_ACTIVITY 1, Dragon.java:66) every leg tucks one radian and holds (:435-450).

The wings branch three ways (:469-477): in flight they beat 50 degrees at 0.75 rad/tick (an 8.4-tick beat), the middle spars 4/3 of that and the tips 3/2, each placed at the end of the spar before (:479-513); on the ground they hang folded at −0.85 with a 5-degree stir, and while the attacking flag is set they half-raise to −0.45 and flap 36 degrees at 0.85 rad/tick.

The tail sways in phase along seven segments, the swing growing toward the tip: 0.45 wide at 0.76 rad/tick in calm flight, 0.75 wide at 0.96 attacking, 0.22 wide at 0.22 on the ground, still in the sitting pose (:516-570). The neck turns a quarter and a half of the look and the head three quarters, the jaws and horns riding it (:592-616); in flight the look is replaced by a filtered turn rate clamped to ±50 degrees (:577-587). The lower jaw chomps 25 degrees at 1.5 rad/tick while attacking and rests at 0.07 (:618-619).

The body blocks and the three back spikes are static; the walk position plays no part. Because the rig is drawn at 0.45, the real-speed leg swing (:429) is the adult's formula at the same 0.32 walk (Dragon.java:133) — the same arc.

The takeoff and the landing are flag flips, the bite is doHurtTarget (Dragon.java:285-302) from the flight AI (:693) or the ridden auto-melee (:591), the shot is shootProjectileAt (:808-832, a SmallFireball at fire level 1) — none of these are animation events.

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelDragon row (geckolib_migration_design.md:446): 'Baby profile uses the same bones at 45% part sizes, never the adult constants' — the adult's bones (head [1,0.8] @1, body [1.4,1.1] @0.5, four leg roots [0.4,0.75] @0.5, wing14/wing15 [2.2,0.5] @0.25, tail1/tail3/tail6 [0.6,0.55] @0.25) each at 0.45: head [0.45,0.36], body [0.63,0.495], leg roots [0.18,0.3375], root panels [0.99,0.225], tail [0.27,0.2475]; the damage factors unchanged. The names resolve as in `dragon`'s seed: head, body, wing14, wing15, tail1, tail3, tail6 as written; 'four leg roots' taken as leg1, leg2 (hind thighs), leg3, leg4 (front uppers). The row pins the baby's renderer x0.45, texture state and root dimensions independently (BabyDragonRenderer.java:34; ModEntities.java:496-497).
